section: common mistakes
text: Common mistakes "The agent is better, so route everything to it." It costs 2,458 tokens per question against 735 here, grows quadratically with searches (section 1), and loses to the pipeline on some questions (53 of 200 here).
label: fat

section: common mistakes
text: In Ferrazzi et al.'s controlled comparison ( arXiv 2601.07711 ) the agentic system used 3.3 times the input tokens and 1.5 times the time, and lost by 64.6 against 87.9 F1 on FEVER; note that the FEVER number there scores user-intent routing (is the question in scope), not fact verification as it is often quoted, including on the old version of this page published. "The second search failed, so retrieval is the problem." The same tool finds the second gold paragraph every time it is given the bridge entity's name (78 of 78), and the 1.7B agent's own queries for 18 of 55.
label: core

section: common mistakes
text: Log the queries; most second-hop failures are query writing. "More context is safer: put everything in the window." The question's own 10 paragraphs, gold included, scored 0.456, the best here; an 8k window of on-topic distractors scored 0.320, below a top-10 search (0.425), at 14.64 s per question.
label: fat

section: common mistakes
text: More is better only until the extra text is mostly near-misses. "The architecture matters more than the prompt." An answer prompt that made the 1.7B answer yes or no to open questions cost the top-5 pipeline 0.249 against 0.402, a larger gap than between any two architectures here.
label: fat

section: common mistakes
text: Count answers of the wrong type before comparing strategies. "Let the evaluator throw away bad results." CRAG-style replacement of results judged incorrect scored 0.332 against 0.402 for keeping them: in a two-hop question the "bad-looking" set often holds the first hop. "A confident top hit means retrieval succeeded." For multi-hop questions it predicted the opposite here (AUROC 0.43 for both gold in the top 5): the search locked onto the first hop.
label: fat

section: common mistakes
text: Evaluate the result set against everything the question needs. "Our router works: accuracy went up and tokens went down." Compare it with sending a random share of the same size to the expensive path.
label: core

section: common mistakes
text: Here the learned and CRAG-style routers did no better than a random split; only a one-line rule (comparison word to the agent) beat always-pipeline, by +0.042. "Score the final answer only." The agent was right 23 times without reading both gold paragraphs, and wrong 47 times with both in hand.
label: fat

section: common mistakes
text: Answer-only metrics cannot separate guessing from grounding or retrieval failures from reading failures. "The window is 128k, so the model uses 128k." RULER's effective length was half the claimed window for GPT-4 and a quarter for Qwen2-72B published; at 32k tokens prefill alone would take about 80 s on this laptop (extrapolated). "Prompt caching makes long agent loops cheap." It cuts the price of re-read tokens and skips their prefill (1,022 of 2,258 tokens computed here), but each step still generates its own output and the window still grows; budgets still matter. "Memory: keep the last few turns." A sliding window kept both gold paragraphs in 1 of 92 multi-hop trajectories; retrieval over the agent's own reads, queried with its current state, kept them in 85.
label: fat
